entries.value: The work I most want to keep doing is the work I'm doing now. At Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus I own major parts of the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system, including the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence models over event streams, and a learning-to-rank layer for ordering alerts. What that project taught me is that detection accuracy is only half the problem. An anomaly system that fires too often creates a second problem instead of solving the first, which is why I also built a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so an analyst can see why something was flagged. That is the kind of engineering I want to build a career around: systems other people depend on in production, where failure modes, prioritization, and explanation quality matter as much as model performance, and where the human still makes the call. Datadog is the clearest place I know of to work on that at a scale I can't reach on my own, and as an intern I'd want to own a real piece of a system rather than isolated tickets.
